title: Object lifecycle: construction, reference and garbage collection

videos.script: Every object in this course was made with new, and none was ever deleted. This lesson follows one object from its first byte to its last. {{construction}} First, what new really does. The object exists, zeroed, before the constructor's first line runs. A loan prints its own fields to prove it. {{reachable}} Then the rule the garbage collector follows. It does not free what you stopped using. It frees what nothing can reach. {{churn}} A program allocates almost two gigabytes in a thirty-two megabyte heap, and finishes. Another keeps everything, and runs out. {{request}} Then System.gc, which asks for a collection, and can be told no. {{finalize}} Last, the cleanup method Java once promised to call, and the reason it is being removed. By the end you can say why an object is still in memory, and what has to be closed by hand.
